43.0.s.en: 1. The glory of the Lord in His temple:

43.0.0.en: 1 Afterward he brought me to the gate, even the gate that looketh toward the east: 2 And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like a noise of many waters: and the earth shined with his glory. 3 And it was according to the appearance of the vision which I saw, even according to the vision that I saw when I came to destroy the city: and the visions were like the vision that I saw by the river Chebar; and I fell upon my face. 4 And the glory of the LORD came into the house by the way of the gate whose prospect is toward the east. 5 So the spirit took me up, and brought me into the inner court; and, behold, the glory of the LORD filled the house. 6 And I heard him speaking unto me out of the house; and the man stood by me.

43.0.1.en: The Spirit took him to the eastern gate [1], to the very place from which the cherubic chariot, God's fiery chariot, had departed to heaven, leaving the house of the Lord (Ezek 10:19) and leaving the whole city (chapter 11). Now the breath returns to the prophet whose whole life had been embittered by the departure of the glory of the Lord from His people, and his mission is crowned with success; indeed the whole book reaches its goal, and God's purpose in us is fulfilled.

43.0.2.en: Without exaggeration we can say that the book of Ezekiel is the book of "the glory of the Lord." The book began with the revelation of this divine glory, and the Spirit of the Lord kept disclosing in every way, in warning, that this glory was departing from the people because of their immersion in idol worship, abominations and the shedding of blood, their acceptance of the counsel of false prophets and false prophetesses, the priests' preoccupation with their own interests at the expense of the flock, and so on... At last the glory of the Lord departed from His temple and His city (chapters 10, 11), since the temple was defiled and the city made unclean, and the Lord chastened His people with captivity, famine and the destruction of their cities, to urge them to repent so that His glory would return to them. Finally the Lord broke the enemy from without (chapters 25-32), and promised them the return of His glory, presenting Himself as a shepherd to them in place of the wicked shepherds (chapter 34), urging them to repent so that they would not die (chapter 36), and promising them the establishment of a new temple, a new city and a new king, a son of David... All of this was for the sake of the return of "the glory of the Lord" in their midst.

43.0.3.en: Truly it is the book of "the glory of the Lord," for this expression occurs 14 times in the first eleven chapters alone!

43.0.4.en: And now he describes this return somewhat briefly, making the following points clear:

43.0.5.en: A. The divine glory came from the east... declaring that the return of the divine glory to human nature is accomplished by the coming of the Lord Christ, who was called the East (Zech 6:12), "the Sun of righteousness" who shines without ceasing to scatter the darkness (Mal 4:2), and whose star appeared in the east (Mt 2:2). Therefore the deacon cries out in the Divine Liturgy, "Look toward the east." The Church has received a tradition of praying, in all her liturgies and in household and personal worship, facing east. Indeed, in Europe some graves have been found built in such a way that the faces of those who repose are toward the east, and the martyrs and saints often looked toward the east as they delivered their spirits to the Lord.

43.0.6.en: B. In the return of the glory of the Lord here, the cloud did not appear as it did in the tabernacle of meeting or the temple of Solomon (Ex 40:34-35; 1 Kgs 8:10), for His glory in His new Church is not declared through the cloud of types and shadows but through the only-begotten Son Himself, since humanity meets the Father in His Son without hindrance!

43.1.0.en: C. The glory of the Lord appeared through two things: the power of the word and radiance, as it says: "The glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like a noise of many waters: and the earth shined with his glory" [2]. His word is effective and powerful, declared like the noise of many waters, that is, it works in the midst of many peoples (the waters) and nations to draw them to Him; and the effect of this glory is enlightenment, so that the earth that lived a time under darkness shines. As St. Paul says: "For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord: walk as children of light" (Eph 5:8). "Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son" (Col 1:13). And St. Peter says: "But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light" (1 Pet 2:9).

43.2.0.en: D. He saw the same glory that he had seen by the river Chebar (chapter 1), and as he fell the first time on his face (Ezek 1:28) until the Spirit of the Lord entered him and set him up to speak with him (Ezek 2:2), so here he fell on his face [3] and the Spirit of the Lord carried him to the inner court. No one can enjoy the divine glory and enter into its vision and the hearing of the voice of the Lord without the Holy Spirit, whom the Lord promised, saying: "He shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you" (Jn 16:14).

43.2.1.en: Rightly the commentators consider Ezekiel the prophet of the Holy Spirit, as they call Isaiah the prophet of the Son and Jeremiah the prophet of the Father... For there is no discourse of the prophet Ezekiel in which the work of the Spirit is not declared.

43.3.0.en: 7 And he said unto me, Son of man, the place of my throne, and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel for ever, and my holy name, shall the house of Israel no more defile, neither they, nor their kings, by their whoredom, nor by the carcases of their kings in their high places. 8 In their setting of their threshold by my thresholds, and their post by my posts, and the wall between me and them, they have even defiled my holy name by their abominations that they have committed: wherefore I have consumed them in mine anger. 9 Now let them put away their whoredom, and the carcases of their kings, far from me, and I will dwell in the midst of them for ever. 10 Thou son of man, shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern. 11 And if they be ashamed of all that they have done, shew them the form of the house, and the fashion thereof, and the goings out thereof, and the comings in thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the laws thereof: and write it in their sight, that they may keep the whole form thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and do them. 12 This is the law of the house; Upon the top of the mountain the whole limit thereof round about shall be most holy. Behold, this is the law of the house.

43.3.1.en: A. The return of the glory of the Lord once more to His temple as the place of His throne and the place of the soles of His feet, to dwell in the midst of His people for ever [7], was truly accomplished by the coming of the incarnate only-begotten Son among us, when He "hath broken down the middle wall of partition, that is, the enmity" (Eph 2:14-15). This divine work is accomplished through the renewal of the divine covenant with man; in it the Father offered His only Son as an atonement for our sins, and in it we too are committed to walk as befits this great work, by the working of His divine grace. Therefore God warns His people once again not to defile His holy name, they or their kings [7], lest this be counted contempt of God's long-suffering and love. Our teacher the Apostle Paul says: "Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace? For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people. It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God" (Heb 10:29-31).

43.4.0.en: B. If God declared to them the return of His glory in order to raise in them the spirit of hope, yet in order to enjoy this and to learn the measures of the temple and the mysteries of His house, His ordinances and His sacraments, they must first repent [9-11]: "Now let them put away their whoredom, and the carcases of their kings, far from me, and I will dwell in the midst of them for ever" [9]. Repentance is the way of entry into God's dwelling in our midst and the knowledge of His divine mysteries.

43.5.0.en: C. When His house is sanctified, the whole mountain is sanctified, for He says: "This is the law of the house; Upon the top of the mountain the whole limit thereof round about shall be most holy" [12]. Let us be concerned with the sanctification of the heart, and the whole body will be sanctified; and let our souls be sanctified, and God will sanctify those who are around us! The true believer is a mystery of blessing to those around him!

43.6.0.en: 13 And these are the measures of the altar after the cubits: The cubit is a cubit and an hand breadth; even the bottom shall be a cubit, and the breadth a cubit, and the border thereof by the edge thereof round about shall be a span: and this shall be the higher place of the altar. 14 And from the bottom upon the ground even to the lower settle shall be two cubits, and the breadth one cubit; and from the lesser settle even to the greater settle shall be four cubits, and the breadth one cubit. 15 So the altar shall be four cubits; and from the altar and upward shall be four horns. 16 And the altar shall be twelve cubits long, twelve broad, square in the four squares thereof. 17 And the settle shall be fourteen cubits long and fourteen broad in the four squares thereof; and the border about it shall be half a cubit; and the bottom thereof shall be a cubit about; and his stairs shall look toward the east.

43.6.1.en: When he spoke of the return of the glory of the Lord, he spoke first of repentance as the way of entering into the holy places, yet through the holy sacrifice. Therefore he followed the return of the glory of the Lord with the discourse on the altar of burnt offering... as though the sacrifice were the foundation for the entry of the divine glory into our life. As Father Methodius of Olympus says: [The Church grows day by day in stature and beauty through her cooperation and union with the Logos, who descends to us even now and continues His descent to us in the remembrance of His sufferings.] And St. John Chrysostom says of the sacrifice of the Lord Christ, that is, the Eucharist: [By it the soul is purified, and by it it is adorned and set aflame.] It is noticed that the altar here is larger than it was before, that is, before the captivity (Ezra 3:3); its size is thus: 6 square yards at the top, 7 square yards at the bottom, and a height of 4.5 yards. It has a ledge rising one yard above the ground, on which some priests sit for service, and another ledge two more yards away on which other priests sit. The sacrifice is presented to those on the first ledge, who hand it over to those on the second ledge to place it on the altar.

43.7.0.en: 18 And he said unto me, Son of man, thus saith the Lord GOD; These are the ordinances of the altar in the day when they shall make it, to offer burnt offerings thereon, and to sprinkle blood thereon. 19 And thou shalt give to the priests the Levites that be of the seed of Zadok, which approach unto me, to minister unto me, saith the Lord GOD, a young bullock for a sin offering. 20 And thou shalt take of the blood thereof, and put it on the four horns of it, and on the four corners of the settle, and upon the border round about: thus shalt thou cleanse and purge it. 21 Thou shalt take the bullock also of the sin offering, and he shall burn it in the appointed place of the house, without the sanctuary. 22 And on the second day thou shalt offer a kid of the goats without blemish for a sin offering; and they shall cleanse the altar, as they did cleanse it with the bullock. 23 When thou hast made an end of cleansing it, thou shalt offer a young bullock without blemish, and a ram out of the flock without blemish. 24 And thou shalt offer them before the LORD, and the priests shall cast salt upon them, and they shall offer them up for a burnt offering unto the LORD. 25 Seven days shalt thou prepare every day a goat for a sin offering: they shall also prepare a young bullock, and a ram out of the flock, without blemish. 26 Seven days shall they purge the altar and purify it; and they shall consecrate themselves. 27 And when these days are expired, it shall be, that upon the eighth day, and so forward, the priests shall make your burnt offerings upon the altar, and your peace offerings; and I will accept you, saith the Lord GOD.

43.8.0.en: Consecration requires a daily sacrifice for seven days [25], a reference to the unceasing sacrificial work of the Lord Christ throughout all the days of our sojourn, or throughout the week of our life, and thus the complete removal of our sins, so that they have no place in us all the days of our sojourn.

43.9.0.en: God's acceptance of them begins on the eighth day [27], as though the secret of the Lord's acceptance of us is that we enter with the Lord Christ into the new heavenly life (the eighth day, that is, after the week, or the first day of the new week), which is the day of the resurrection of the Lord Christ from the dead; in it we rise and are justified before the Father and are counted with Him as sitting in the heavenly places.

43.9.1.en: As for the salting of the sacrifice [24], it is a reference to divine grace, as the Apostle says: "Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man" (Col 4:6). The grace of God is the salt that seasons the tongue and all the members of the body, its senses and feelings, as it seasons the soul with all its powers, and the mind.

43.9.2.en: Finally, those who minister at it are the seed of Zadok [19], whom He called those who approach Him. For Zadok means "righteous one" or "just," so there is no approach to God's altar except through enjoying the righteousness of Christ, that we may be in His eyes of the seed of Zadok spiritually.

43.9.4.en: *How great was the joy of Your prophet Ezekiel!

43.9.6.en: Your glory that departed from the temple and the city has returned!

43.9.8.en: So may You shine in me, O Sun of righteousness!

43.9.9.en: May You scatter my darkness with Your marvellous light!

43.9.10.en: *May You dwell with Your glory, not through the cloud, through types and shadows, but by the indwelling of Your Holy Spirit in me!

43.9.11.en: *By the coming of Your glory there was a voice like many waters, and the earth shined and was filled with radiance!

43.9.12.en: May You dwell in me with Your glory, so that Your voice thunders within me, and all the foundations of evil shake before You!

43.9.13.en: You shine with Your radiance in my depths, and I enjoy a surpassing spiritual beauty!

43.9.14.en: May Your glory dwell within me, for I confess my guilt to You, and complain to You of my shame!

43.9.15.en: For I know that repentance is the way of Your royal glory!

43.9.16.en: And holiness is the eye that sees Your radiance!

43.9.17.en: *Set up Your altar in me, and sanctify it with Your precious Blood!

43.9.18.en: Your glory is bound to Your Cross!

43.9.19.en: Here I carry it by You and with You, O You who bore the sins of the whole world by Your Cross!

44.0.0.en: 1 Then he brought me back the way of the gate of the outward sanctuary which looketh toward the east; and it was shut. 2 Then said the LORD unto me; This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter in by it; because the LORD, the God of Israel, hath entered in by it, therefore it shall be shut. 3 It is for the prince; the prince, he shall sit in it to eat bread before the LORD; he shall enter by the way of the porch of that gate, and shall go out by the way of the same.

44.0.1.en: For the third time the Spirit of the Lord brings him to the eastern gate, but he finds it closed, and the Lord assures him:

44.0.2.en: "This gate shall be shut, it shall not be opened, and no man shall enter in by it; because the LORD, the God of Israel, hath entered in by it, therefore it shall be shut.

44.0.3.en: The Prince, the Prince, he shall sit in it to eat bread before the LORD.

44.1.0.en: He shall enter by the way of the porch of that gate, and shall go out by the way of the same" [2-3].

44.1.1.en: When he speaks of those who work in the temple, he begins by speaking of the Lord Christ, as He is the first and last worker in the temple, in whom all His priests and servants are hidden. Him He called "the Prince, the Prince," as though saying that He is the summit of those who work in the temple, or the greatest High Priest. The word is repeated twice because He is the worker in the Old Testament as the invisible Word of God, and He is the worker in the New Testament as the incarnate Word of God. Therefore He passed through the east gate to go up the seven steps to the outer court (Ezek 40:22) and then the eight steps to the inner court (Ezek 40:27), as though He shone upon us with His light in the Old Testament (7 steps) through types and shadows, and then returned and shone upon us with His light in the New Testament (8 steps) by His divine incarnation... He opened for us the mysteries of the Old and New Testaments, at one time through the Law and the prophets and at another through the Gospel.

44.1.2.en: What is the closed gate through which the Lord entered and went out and which remained closed, but the virginal womb of St. Mary, in which the Lord dwelt, becoming incarnate of her by the Holy Spirit and being born of her, while she remained a virgin?! St. Jerome says in this regard: [She (Mary) is the eastern gate of which Ezekiel spoke, which is always closed, always shining, and sealed, and at the same time proclaims the Holy of Holies; through it enters and goes out "the Sun of righteousness" (Mal 4:2), who is a high priest after the order of Melchisedec" (Heb 5:10). Let him who criticizes me explain to me how Jesus entered through the closed doors when He allowed His hands and side to be touched, showing that He had bones and flesh (Jn 10:19, 27), proving that He bore a real body and not an imaginary one, and then let him explain how St. Mary can be a mother and a virgin at the same time!] We have already spoken of the perpetual virginity of the Virgin Mary in our book "St. Mary in the Orthodox Concept."

44.1.3.en: As for His saying, "He shall sit in it to eat bread before the LORD," it contains a reference to the divine Incarnation, in which the Son of God became man.

44.2.0.en: 4 Then brought he me the way of the north gate before the house: and I looked, and, behold, the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD: and I fell upon my face. 5 And the LORD said unto me, Son of man, mark well, and behold with thine eyes, and hear with thine ears all that I say unto thee concerning all the ordinances of the house of the LORD, and all the laws thereof; and mark well the entering in of the house, with every going forth of the sanctuary. 6 And thou shalt say to the rebellious, even to the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; O ye house of Israel, let it suffice you of all your abominations, 7 In that ye have brought into my sanctuary strangers, uncircumcised in heart, and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, to pollute it, even my house, when ye offer my bread, the fat and the blood, and they have broken my covenant because of all your abominations. 8 And ye have not kept the charge of mine holy things: but ye have set keepers of my charge in my sanctuary for yourselves. 9 Thus saith the Lord GOD; No stranger, uncircumcised in heart, nor uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of any stranger that is among the children of Israel. 10 And the Levites that are gone away far from me, when Israel went astray, which went astray away from me after their idols; they shall even bear their iniquity. 11 Yet they shall be ministers in my sanctuary, having charge at the gates of the house, and ministering to the house: they shall slay the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before them to minister unto them. 12 Because they ministered unto them before their idols, and caused the house of Israel to fall into iniquity; therefore have I lifted up mine hand against them, saith the Lord GOD, and they shall bear their iniquity. 13 And they shall not come near unto me, to do the office of a priest unto me, nor to come near to any of my holy things, in the most holy place: but they shall bear their shame, and their abominations which they have committed. 14 But I will make them keepers of the charge of the house, for all the service thereof, and for all that shall be done therein.

44.2.1.en: The Lord entered His house with His glory by the eastern gate, which He kept closed so that no other might enter by it, but He left the other doors open to every person who desires union with Him. Yet the Lord did not leave these doors, wide for all and open by His divine love, without a guard, but appointed the Levites as guards over them.

44.2.2.en: In a firm rebuke the Lord disclosed to the Levites their past errors, not only that they might remedy them and not fall into them in the future, but rather that they might compensate for the wicked years that are past by positive striving for the sake of the Kingdom of God. It is as though their repentance does not stop at their ceasing from evil, but rather obliges them to use the energies, gifts, time and so on... that were working for evil, so that they may be used for the sake of the Kingdom of God.

44.2.3.en: He limited their errors to two:

44.3.0.en: First: their negligence in guarding the house of the Lord, guarding His holy things and setting guards to keep these holy things for them [8], so that strangers uncircumcised in heart and flesh together entered His house and defiled it! Nothing is more bitter to God's heart than that the priests and servants neglect the house of the Lord, until the very place in which the mystery of holiness lies becomes a place of evil! The Lord has warned much in both Testaments that whoever corrupts the temple of God, the Lord will corrupt him, and that whoever suffers the woman Jezebel to seduce his children and corrupt his holy things, the Lord will shake his lampstand. I say this with bitterness, because we often make light of the holy things of the Lord and confuse love and gentleness with laxity regarding the holy things. Our love for sinners and our gentleness toward them do not mean laxity on our part regarding the holy things of the Lord.

44.3.1.en: Likewise, the Levites' negligence in guarding obliges them, by repentance, to return to guarding the house of the Lord [1].

44.4.0.en: Second: the Levites ministered to the people during idol worship and caused them to stumble [10]; therefore it was necessary for them, by repentance, to sacrifice to the Lord for the people in order to restore those who stumbled. It is as though in our repentance it is fitting for us not only to turn back from our falls, but also to restore those who stumbled because of us, through our holy ministry to them in the Lord.

44.5.0.en: 15 But the priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, that kept the charge of my sanctuary when the children of Israel went astray from me, they shall come near to me to minister unto me, and they shall stand before me to offer unto me the fat and the blood, saith the Lord GOD: 16 They shall enter into my sanctuary, and they shall come near to my table, to minister unto me, and they shall keep my charge. 17 And it shall come to pass, that when they enter in at the gates of the inner court, they shall be clothed with linen garments; and no wool shall come upon them, whiles they minister in the gates of the inner court, and within. 18 They shall have linen bonnets upon their heads, and shall have linen breeches upon their loins; they shall not gird themselves with any thing that causeth sweat. 19 And when they go forth into the utter court, even into the utter court to the people, they shall put off their garments wherein they ministered, and lay them in the holy chambers, and they shall put on other garments; and they shall not sanctify the people with their garments. 20 Neither shall they shave their heads, nor suffer their locks to grow long; they shall only poll their heads. 21 Neither shall any priest drink wine, when they enter into the inner court. 22 Neither shall they take for their wives a widow, nor her that is put away: but they shall take maidens of the seed of the house of Israel, or a widow that had a priest before. 23 And they shall teach my people the difference between the holy and profane, and cause them to discern between the unclean and the clean. 24 And in controversy they shall stand in judgment; and they shall judge it according to my judgments: and they shall keep my laws and my statutes in all mine assemblies; and they shall hallow my sabbaths. 25 And they shall come at no dead person to defile themselves: but for father, or for mother, or for son, or for daughter, for brother, or for sister that hath had no husband, they may defile themselves. 26 And after he is cleansed, they shall reckon unto him seven days. 27 And in the day that he goeth into the sanctuary, unto the inner court, to minister in the sanctuary, he shall offer his sin offering, saith the Lord GOD. 28 And it shall be unto them for an inheritance: I am their inheritance: and ye shall give them no possession in Israel: I am their possession. 29 They shall eat the meat offering, and the sin offering, and the trespass offering: and every dedicated thing in Israel shall be theirs. 30 And the first of all the firstfruits of all things, and every oblation of all, of every sort of your oblations, shall be the priest's: ye shall also give unto the priest the first of your dough, that he may cause the blessing to rest in thine house. 31 The priests shall not eat of any thing that is dead of itself, or torn, whether it be fowl or beast.

44.5.1.en: God chose the sons of Zadok alone, those who truly kept the holy charge when the people went astray; therefore they alone were worthy to approach His holy altar and minister at His table. The Lord took care to lay down for them a law of their own that deals with many matters of their life, among them:

44.6.0.en: A. Dress: "When they enter in at the gates of the inner court, they shall be clothed with linen garments; and no wool shall come upon them, whiles they minister" [17]. They wear linen during the service as a sign of purity and cleanness, and they do not wear wool. Perhaps wool was forbidden for fear that it might come from a dead animal, for He does not want His servants to enter His holy places bearing any trace of anything dead. He also gave a reason for not wearing wool, namely, lest they "sweat" [18], for the servant of the altar must be active, working with vigor, because whoever sweats is concerned for his body and becomes sluggish.

44.6.1.en: He also required them to put off the garments of service, in which they sanctify, in their own holy chambers, for it is not fitting to go out in these holy garments while attending to their temporal needs.

44.6.2.en: Wearing the linen garments of service in the holy places of the Lord signifies our putting on the Lord Christ Himself, because He alone is the Good Shepherd, the High Priest of good things to come; by Him and in Him we carry out the priestly and pastoral work.

44.6.3.en: B. Shaving the hair: He asked them not to go to extremes, neither to shave it completely like the priests of the Gentiles, nor to leave it as it is like the Nazirites, but to trim it with moderation. For if the priest of the New Testament consecrates his heart and life completely to the ministry, yet he behaves with moderation even in his appearance, being an example to the people, able to win many by his conduct, which expresses his fellowship with God.

44.7.0.en: C. Food and drink: He asked them not to drink anything intoxicating when they enter for the service [21]. In the New Testament the Apostle Paul says: "A bishop must be... not given to wine" (1 Tim 3:1, 3). St. Jerome comments: [Indulgence in wine is among the faults of the gluttonous and the luxurious. When the body is heated with wine, lust immediately rises in it. Drinking wine means indulging oneself, and this means sensual luxury, and sensual luxury means the breaking of chastity. The person who lives in luxury is dead while he lives (1 Tim 5:6). But he who drinks wine is not dead but buried. One hour of dissipation made Noah uncovered after he had been covered for sixty years with dignity (Gen 9:20-21).]

44.8.0.en: The Lord asked the priests not to eat of any dead animal or bird, nor of what is torn [31]. He wants the priest to be pure of soul; his acceptance of eating something dead or torn is a sign of baseness of soul. Perhaps He also wanted by this that the priest should live on the word of God, which refreshes and sanctifies his body and spirit, rejecting the teachings of the heretics, which make his body (symbolized by the animal) and his soul (symbolized by the bird) dead or torn by Satan. Let the priest draw from the living spiritual springs, lest germs seep into his life and pass to his people.

44.8.1.en: D. Marriage: The priest is bound to observe the dignity of his priestly work, so he does not marry a widow or a divorced woman, lest anyone doubt his integrity. He was only permitted to marry the widow of a priest who had departed [22].

44.8.2.en: In the Coptic Church the priest never marries after receiving the sacrament of the priesthood, for he has become a father, who looks on all girls and women as his daughters, and a father does not marry his daughter.

44.8.3.en: E. Preaching: It is fitting for the priest to be able to teach, so that he teaches his people "the difference between the unclean and the clean" [33]; and to be just in his judgment: "They shall judge it according to my judgments: and they shall keep my laws and my statutes in all mine assemblies; and they shall hallow my sabbaths" [24].

44.8.4.en: F. Concerning teaching, St. John Chrysostom says: [The Apostle showed what pertains to the bishop, that he be "apt to teach" (1 Tim 3:3). What is asked of those under his care is very essential for him who takes up the pastoral care.]

44.8.5.en: G. His mourning for the dead: God asked the priest not to touch a dead person lest he be defiled, but He permitted him to touch his father or mother or son or daughter or brother or sister... and he remains a week being purified and offers a sin offering so that he may minister in the Holy Place.

44.8.6.en: He wants to lift the priest above everything temporal, to bind his heart to the heavenly things, so that he does not grieve over anyone's departure; yet He took account of the relatives mentioned because of the human feelings that we cannot ignore in the priest's life.

44.8.7.en: H. Their support: God did not allow His priests to receive a share of inheritance with their brethren in the Promised Land, but He came forward to them to be Himself their inheritance; He is bound to satisfy all their spiritual, psychological and bodily needs. He asked the rest of the tribes to give them tithes and firstfruits as though they were offered to God Himself.

44.8.8.en: The scholar Origen comments on the Lord's saying to them that He is their inheritance [28], saying: [Their portion is not on the earth, but the Lord Himself is their portion, for it is said of Him that He is their portion and inheritance. They represent those who did not fail because of the obstacles of bodily nature, but passed beyond the glory of visible things and placed in the Lord their whole life with all its arrangements, those who do not seek bodily things, or things foreign to reason, but sought wisdom and the knowledge of the mysteries of God. And where their treasure is, there will their heart be also (Mt 6:21). So they have no inheritance on the earth, but rose on high, higher than heaven; there they are with the Lord for ever in His Word and His wisdom and the delight of knowing Him, satisfied with His sweetness, so that He is their food, their shelter, their wealth and their kingdom. This is their destiny, and these are the possessions they know, with regard to those for whom God is their only inheritance.]

44.8.9.en: This concerns God being their inheritance; as for the firstfruits, all of them are theirs [30]. The scholar Origen comments on this matter, saying: [The Law commands that the firstfruits of the fruits and the animals be offered to the priests. So whoever possesses a field or a vineyard or an olive grove or a garden, or does any work on the land, or raises even the smallest livestock, must offer all the firstfruits to God through the priests, for Scripture says that what is given to the priests is offered to God. By this we learn from the Law that it is not lawful to benefit from the fruits of the earth, nor from the animals, even the small tame ones, unless we offer all the firstfruits to God through the priests. In my opinion this law, like many other laws, must be observed even in its literal meaning.]

44.8.10.en: And the scholar Origen lifts our spiritual mind to see in the Lord Christ Himself the greatest Priest to whom spiritual firstfruits are offered, such as the firstfruits of Asia (Rom 16:5) and the firstfruits of Achaia (Rom 16:5), and such as Cornelius, who was offered as a firstfruit, being the firstborn not only of the church of Caesarea but of all the Gentiles. The celibates and virgins (Rev 14:4) are counted as firstfruits offered to the greatest High Priest, our Lord Jesus Christ, not only those who are virgins in body but also those who are virgins in spirit, like the wise virgins who were waiting for the Bridegroom at midnight. And the scholar Origen says: [As we have said, let each of us desire to grow until he reaches the point of being chosen from among the firstfruits, so as to be offered to God and be the portion of the Lord.]

44.8.11.en: As for the secret of our being firstfruits, it is our union with the Lord Christ, the true "Firstborn." In Him we have become firstfruits and are counted to God the Father as the portion of His greatest Priest, Jesus Christ. Therefore the Lord Christ also offers Himself on our behalf as the firstborn to God. The scholar Origen says: [He was called the firstborn (1 Cor 15:5-23), the firstfruits of those who slept (Rev 19:6). And as He is called King of kings and Lord of lords and Shepherd of shepherds and High Priest (1 Pet 5:4; Heb 5:14), we can call Him "Firstfruit of the firstfruits." He is the firstfruit that is offered not to the high priest but to God Himself, for He "hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour" (Eph 5:2), and after His resurrection from the dead: "sitteth on the right hand of God" (Col 3:1).]

44.8.12.en: In the Old Testament a person was bound to offer the firstfruits to God through the priests so that the Lord would be pleased with him, and the priests ate the firstfruits or used and consumed them. But in the New Testament God offers us the Firstborn, "Jesus Christ"; He offers Him to His people to receive Him, so that they eat His body and partake of His precious Blood and receive His life in Him, not to consume Him but to enjoy the power of His resurrection, which gives us life. Therefore the scholar Origen says: [The firstfruit that was offered in the Law was consumed as food... but as for us, the more we eat of this food, the more abundant we find it!]

44.8.13.en: The Prince who works in the temple

44.8.14.en: * You are the Prince who enters the temple while the gate is closed; You enter and sit in it, and the gate remains closed!

44.8.15.en: You are the Virgin-born of the Virgin, and her virginity remained perpetual!

44.8.16.en: Enter into my depths, O You who work in me; enter and sit, You who hold the key of the heart!

44.8.17.en: Enter into it and close my door before all evil!

44.8.18.en: Who works in the temple of my heart but You?!

44.8.19.en: Who can sanctify it but You?!

44.8.20.en: * Who are the Levite guards within me but those gifts that come from You, which You sanctify and cultivate in me?!

44.8.21.en: Grant them, by repentance, to be faithful in their guarding. * You are the greatest High Priest; You have made us kings and priests to Your holy Father. Grant us the white linen garments, that we may not be defiled!

44.8.22.en: Keep us in our spiritual eating and drinking, and let us not be immersed in the luxury and drunkenness of the world!

44.8.23.en: Allow us to be united with You as a holy bride without a branch!

44.8.24.en: Truly, what portion have I but You?!

44.8.25.en: For You are my life, my resurrection and my treasure!

44.8.26.en: To whom shall I offer myself as a portion but to You, who are all love?!
